thread:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: High 5xx rate observed in prod-west-1. Alert: SLO-error-rate.p95 exceeded (current 4.8% vs SLO 1%). Pager to @taylor (primary) and @jin (secondary). Link: https://monitoring.redwood/prod-west-1/alerts/4962

ops-bot: Incident severity: P2. Auto-creation: incident/1965432100. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/http-5xx-response.md

 taylor: seeing it in grafana now. rolling deploy to prod-west started ~10m ago. low traffic but error burst looks correlated with specific model variant.

 jin: thanks — I'm grabbing logs and trying ``kubectl -n prod-west get pods -l app=inference -o wide`` to see pod restarts. any idea which model?

 taylor: early signal points to model-id "m-velox-3b-q" on nodepool-gpu-a. should be able to test by routing a small batch to fallback model.

 amar: i'm on standby but mid-handoff window ends in 8m. if this needs sustained coverage can one of you take primary after handoff?

 taylor: I can hold primary for another 20m, then jin takes over. Amar, please be secondary after your handoff if you can.

 samira: quick customer impact check: error spike started at +1965432065, affects streaming generation endpoints; estimated 4% of requests saw 5xx, mostly short failures (timeout/503). No billing impact yet but UX on some sessions degraded.

 leo: proposing temporary alert tuning: suppress page for ErrorRate.p95 for 10m and bump threshold to 3% while we validate rollback/fallback. We should record this change in the incident timeline and restore automatically.

 jin: +1 to suppression for noise during rollback testing. How do we do that safely?

 taylor: runbook step: use the alert-manager UI -> Select rule SLO-error-rate.p95 -> Silence for 10m with note "testing fallback/mv rollback". I'll make the suppress and add a comment with the incident id.

 ops-bot: NOTE: any manual silence must be documented. Silence created by taylor at 1965432158 for 10m: reason "testing fallback/mv rollback".

 jin: checked pods — 3 pods in nodepool-gpu-a show OOM+restart counts recent. stack traces point to tokenizer memory spike around long-context requests. Might be a model-specific memory leak/regression from the build pushed in the rolling deploy.

 amar: can we route traffic to m-velox-3b-q-fallback or to m-velox-3b-quantized variant? Would reduce mem pressure while preserving accuracy.

 taylor: yes. I'll flip routing for prod-west to fallback version for 10% of traffic to verify. command I ran: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/reroute -d '{"from":"m-velox-3b-q","to":"m-velox-3b-q-fallback","percent":10}'`` — monitoring now.

 samira: customer impact update: error rate dropped to 2.1% after routing change, latency slightly higher for fallback but acceptable. Logged customers affected list in incident ticket.

 leo: good. Let's formalize: set temporary SLO threshold to 3% and silence pages for 15m total while we complete rollback. We will also create a follow-up to revert the silence and run a postmortem.

 taylor: agreed. I'll create a postmortem stub in the incident ticket and assign action items. jin will lead root cause, amar will validate config for circuit-breakers, samira will compile customer list.

 jin: starting deeper heap / mem profiling now. pulling traces into S3: s3://incidents/1965432100/traces.

 ops-bot: Reminder: handoff schedule: amar's handoff window ends in 6m. With current plan, taylor remains primary until 1965432300, jin becomes primary at 1965432310, amar becomes secondary.

 amar: confirmed, will take secondary after my handoff. if anything spikes again ping me directly.

 taylor: adding runbook pointer in timeline: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/http-5xx-response.md#model-regressions — follow step "fallback route" + "silence alert".

 leo: after rollback completes, we should also consider lowering batching on the variant for a day and enabling KV-cache guardrail to avoid tokenization memory spikes. I'll propose follow-up config change in the infra backlog.

 samira: logging this as SLO-tweak: temporary threshold 3% from 1965432158 to 1965433058, silence created. Will include this in customer-facing incident summary.

 taylor: closing loop — suppression will be removed automatically at 1965432758, but I will verify and manually restore if needed. If anyone needs write access to the silence, DM me. :thumbsup:
